newsitem.title: USA: Dow Chemical cleared in Michigan implant case.
newsitem.headline: Dow Chemical cleared in Michigan implant case.

text.p: A judge ruled Thursday that Dow Chemical Co. is not liable for medical problems that hundreds of Michigan women claimed arose from silicone gel breast implants, the third such state court victory for the giant chemical company.

According to Dow Chemical, Wayne County Circuit Judge Robert Colombo Jr., rejected plaintiff claims that implant maker Dow Corning Corp. had relied on Dow Chemical to establish the safety of silicone for use in the implants.
Dow Chemical did not make silicone for the implants, although it says it did conduct silicone tests for its co-owned Dow Corning venture that were unrelated to breast implants.

Dow Corning is jointly owned Dow Chemical and Corning Inc. Once the world's largest maker of breast implants filled with silicone gel, Dow Corning filed for bankruptcy-law protection from creditors two years ago because of the claims it was facing.
Appellate courts in New York and California have upheld lower court rulings that also said Dow Chemical was not liable.
The company said the Michigan decision affects about 800 cases filed against it in the state. More than 3,000 silicone implant cases against Dow Chemical have been dismissed, it said.
"Naturally, the plaintiffs are disappointed," said David Black, one of the lead plaintiff attorneys. "I'm sure we're going to seriously look at filing an appeal to the Michigan Court of Appeals."
Thousands of women with silicone gel implants have filed lawsuits against manufacturers alleging the implants caused connective tissue and immune system problems, as well as other ailments.
Unless Colombo's ruling is reversed, Black said it was likely that Michigan women will only have the bankruptcy case from which to seek remedies.

Colombo's action was the second time he dismissed Michigan claims against Dow Chemical. After his first decision in April 1994, U.S. District Court Judge Sam Pointer, who is overseeing all federal breast implant cases, amended an earlier ruling that opened the door for plaintiffs to refile their state claims.
Black said plaintiffs did that by amending the original master complaint.
